comparisons.peer_topic: Commercial Real Estate Portfolio Composition and Concentration
comparisons.peer_summary: Commercial real estate loans decreased $7.1 billion in 2024 to $65.7 billion, with office representing the largest property type concentration at 23% and California the largest state concentration at 21%.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and BAC disclose concentrations in commercial real estate office sectors. GS reports that 2% of its real estate equity securities are concentrated in office properties as of December 2024. BAC reports that office loans represent the largest property type concentration at 23% of its commercial real estate portfolio. Both disclosures highlight office exposure, but BAC quantifies it as a loan percentage while GS quantifies it as an alternative equity allocation percentage.

sentences.text: • The concentrations for real estate equity securities as of December 2024 were 14% for multifamily (13% as of December 2023), 5% for mixed use (8% as of December 2023), 3% for industrials (3% as of December 2023), 2% for office (2% as of December 2023) and 3% for other real estate equity securities (4% as of December 2023).

Office loans represented the largest property type concentration at 23 percent of the commercial real estate portfolio at December 31, 2024, and approximately one percent of total loans for the Corporation.

comparisons.peer_topic: Real Estate Exposure and Criticized Assets Changes
comparisons.peer_summary: Real Estate exposure was $207.1 billion as of December 31, 2024. Criticized exposure increased by $3.2 billion to $12.4 billion, driven by downgrades primarily in Multifamily and Office.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and JPM disclose concentration and risk data for real estate assets, though GS focuses on alternative equity holdings while JPM focuses on loan exposure. GS reports real estate equity security concentrations by property type, such as 14% multifamily and 2% office. JPM reports total real estate exposure of $207.1 billion and highlights that criticized exposure increases were driven primarily by multifamily and office sectors, indicating shared focus on these specific property types despite different asset classes (equity vs. loans).

sentences.text: • The concentrations for real estate equity securities as of December 2024 were 14% for multifamily (13% as of December 2023), 5% for mixed use (8% as of December 2023), 3% for industrials (3% as of December 2023), 2% for office (2% as of December 2023) and 3% for other real estate equity securities (4% as of December 2023).
Criticized exposure increased by $3.2 billion from $9.2 billion at December 31, 2023 to $12.4 billion at December 31, 2024, predominantly driven by downgrades, primarily in Multifamily and Office.

comparisons.peer_topic: Equity price and correlation risk exposure
comparisons.peer_summary: Exposure to equity price, correlation, and implied volatility risk stems from market-making in equity securities and derivatives, including less liquid positions in non-public entities like private equity and real estate funds.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and MS disclose exposures to private equity and real estate equity securities within their alternative or non-public investment portfolios. GS quantifies the composition, reporting $12.6 billion in private equity and specific real estate equity concentrations (e.g., 14% multifamily) as of December 2024. MS qualitatively describes similar exposure risks from market-making and positions in non-public entities like private equity and real estate funds, noting these positions are less liquid than listed equities.

sentences.text: • Equity securities included $12.6 billion as of December 2024 and $12.1 billion as of December 2023 of private equity positions, and $0.8 billion as of December 2024 and $1.1 billion as of December 2023 of public equity positions that converted from private equity upon the initial public offerings of the underlying companies.

• The concentrations for real estate equity securities as of December 2024 were 14% for multifamily (13% as of December 2023), 5% for mixed use (8% as of December 2023), 3% for industrials (3% as of December 2023), 2% for office (2% as of December 2023) and 3% for other real estate equity securities (4% as of December 2023).

We are exposed to equity price, correlation and implied volatility risk as a result of making markets in equity securities and derivatives and maintaining other positions, including positions in non-public entities.
Positions in non-public entities may include, but are not limited to, exposures to private equity, venture capital, private partnerships, real estate funds and other funds.
